column3: Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats Jeroboam’s name in the disguise instruction; BSB uses “my wife.”
The Hebrew says to take the provisions “in your hand”; BSB says “with you.”
The Hebrew says that his eyes had become fixed; BSB says they were dim.
The Hebrew narrates her arrival in disguise after the instruction; BSB includes it as the reason within the instruction.
The Hebrew says that he is sent to her with something hard; BSB renders this as “bad news.”

The Hebrew uses “one who urinates against a wall,” “restrained,” and “abandoned”; BSB renders these as “every male” and “both slave and free.”
The Hebrew makes the dogs and birds the active subjects of eating; BSB makes the dead the subjects of passive clauses.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says he will “come to a grave” and that good was found in him toward the LORD; BSB says “receive a proper burial” and makes the LORD the finder.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “beyond the River”; BSB identifies the river as the Euphrates.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew separately says she went and came to Tirzah; BSB combines this as departing for Tirzah.
The Hebrew says “by the hand of His servant”; BSB uses “through His servant.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls the reign “the days that Jeroboam reigned”; BSB uses “the length of Jeroboam’s reign.”
The Hebrew repeats Rehoboam’s name; BSB uses “He” for the second occurrence.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses a singular designation for the male shrine prostitute and says “sons of Israel”; BSB uses plural prostitutes and “Israelites.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats the taking verb three times and says “the king’s house”; BSB condenses the taking clauses and uses “royal palace.”
The Hebrew uses “hand,” “runners,” and “the king’s house”; BSB uses “care,” “guard,” and “royal palace.”
The Hebrew uses pronouns for the items carried and returned; BSB supplies “the shields” and adds “later.”
